note: Simplified one-glance model. Stage indices match architecture.json. Each block event: [stage, text, kind]. kind: new | changed.

lines: One program runs everything: network, mining, EVM and storage.
Miners order transactions and earn new ETH.
Smart contracts run inside the EVM.
plain.why: This is the base design. Every later upgrade changes a part of it.

lines: After 2016 attacks, disk-heavy opcodes cost more gas.
A chain ID stops replay of transactions on other chains.
The DAO fork splits off Ethereum Classic.
plain.why: Ethereum learns to change its rules by social agreement.

lines: New EVM tools: REVERT, CREATE2 and zk-proof checks.
The miner reward drops from 5 to 3 to 2 ETH per block.
plain.why: First zk proofs on-chain. Less new ETH.

lines: Data inside transactions costs 4x less gas.
zk-proof checks get cheaper.
plain.why: Rollups become possible on top of Ethereum.

lines: A proof-of-stake chain starts beside the old chain.
Part of every fee is burned (EIP-1559).
Light clients get sync committees.
plain.why: The new engine warms up. ETH supply can now shrink.

lines: Mining stops. Validators with staked ETH make blocks.
A node becomes two programs, linked by the Engine API.
Outside builders sell full blocks to validators (MEV-Boost).
plain.why: Ethereum swaps its engine without stopping the chain.

lines: Stakers can withdraw their ETH.
Smart wallets launch as apps (ERC-4337).
Blobs: a cheap data lane for rollups, deleted after ~18 days.
Blobs have their own fee market.
Contracts get temporary storage (TSTORE).
Normal wallets can run smart-contract code (EIP-7702).
One validator can hold up to 2,048 ETH.
Blob space doubles: 6 target, 9 max.
Nodes check blob data by sampling small pieces (PeerDAS).
Blob space grows to 14 / 21 in small steps (BPO forks).
Default block gas limit: 60M.
plain.why: More rollup data, without bigger nodes.

lines: Block building moves inside the protocol (ePBS).
Each block lists what it touches, so checks run in parallel.
Storage costs more gas. Gas limit target: 200M.
plain.why: Bigger blocks and less trust in relays. Testnet only.

lines: Validator committees force transactions into blocks (FOCIL).
Accounts choose their own signature rules (frame transactions).
plain.why: Censorship resistance becomes a protocol rule. Planned.

lines: Validators check a zk proof instead of re-running blocks.
A binary state tree lets phones verify the chain.
Fast finality and post-quantum signatures.
